passages.title: Passage 1
passages.instructions:
Questions 1–40

You should spend about 60 minutes on Questions 1–40, which are based on the reading passage below.
passages.body:
Enzymatic Plastic Degradation

A Enzymatic plastic degradation harnesses naturally occurring and engineered proteins to break polymer chains into oligomers and monomers that microorganisms can metabolise. Researchers isolate cutinases and PETases from soil bacteria and fungi, then optimise them through directed evolution for industrial temperatures and mixed-waste streams. Proponents envision biological recycling plants that complement mechanical sorting, reducing reliance on virgin petrochemical feedstocks. Skeptics note that real municipal waste contains additives, dyes, and multilayer films that inhibit enzyme access and reduce yields below commercial thresholds. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.

B PET hydrolases cleave ester bonds in polyethylene terephthalate, producing terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol under mild aqueous conditions. Pilot facilities in Europe and Asia pretreat bottles through washing and micronisation before incubation in stirred reactors with immobilised enzymes on porous supports. Process engineers balance reaction time, enzyme loading, and separation costs to compete with mechanical recycling on price. Contamination with polyvinyl chloride or polyurethane still derails batches, requiring tighter upstream optical sorting and spectroscopic detection than many municipalities currently operate. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes.

C Scientists engineer enzymes by inserting disulfide bridges and adjusting surface charge to resist denaturation above seventy degrees Celsius. Machine learning models predict mutations that widen substrate pockets without collapsing catalytic triads. Whole-cell biocatalysts secrete enzymes in situ, potentially lowering purification expenses, though metabolic burden can slow growth in engineered hosts. The author cautions that laboratory kinetics on pure substrates rarely translate directly to heterogeneous post-consumer flakes coated with food residues and adhesives. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality.

D Lifecycle assessments compare enzyme plants with pyrolysis and gasification routes that handle mixed plastics thermochemically at high energy cost. Biological pathways emit less carbon dioxide when powered by renewable electricity, yet water consumption and effluent treatment add hidden burdens. Downstream polymerisation must restore molecular weight for bottle-to-bottle loops, linking depolymerisation economics to virgin resin prices. Policy makers debate extended producer fees that could subsidise enzymatic hubs until scale reduces unit costs across regional supply chains. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.

E Regulatory agencies classify enzymatically derived monomers as recycled content if mass balance audits verify chain of custody. Brand owners seek certification labels to meet corporate pledges on circular packaging, though greenwashing concerns persist when only a fraction of waste volumes pass through biological lines. Open patent pools could widen access for lower-income countries drowning in imported scrap, yet enzyme suppliers prefer proprietary cocktails tuned to local waste compositions. International standards bodies are drafting testing protocols for residual toxicity in treated effluent discharged to municipal treatment works. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.

F Social implications include job shifts from informal waste picking to mechanised plants that may displace livelihoods unless retraining programmes accompany investment. Community groups near pilot sites request transparency about odour, wastewater, and truck traffic. Unions argue that biological recycling should not excuse continued production of single-use items that overwhelm collection systems regardless of downstream technology. The writer maintains that upstream reduction and redesign remain indispensable partners to any enzymatic breakthrough announced in peer-reviewed journals. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality.

G Looking ahead, enzymatic degradation may niche-fill streams where mechanical recycling quality is poor, but it will not magically dissolve global plastic pollution. Success depends on collection infrastructure, design for recyclability, and honest accounting of energy and water inputs. If marketing races ahead of deployed capacity, the author fears public cynicism will follow, undermining legitimate advances. Integrated strategies that combine policy, material innovation, and credible scaling timelines offer a more plausible path than betting on enzymes alone. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.
